title: The Fourteenth Constable: The Broken Ceramic Shard
full_text:
The Fourteenth Constable spoke:

'A jewelry shop was burgled at night, and the thief dropped a heavy earthen oil lamp upon the cobblestones in his haste, shattering it into twenty fragments.

I gathered the broken ceramic pieces, noticing that the clay was of an unusual red-and-white marbled texture with a peculiar maker’s stamp: a crescent with three dots.

I visited all eighteen potteries in Cairo until I found the master potter who owned that stamp: he testified that he had sold three marbled lamps to an artisan in the leather-workers' lane.

We inspected the suspect's workshop: upon his shelf sat the broken base of the lamp, and the shard found at the crime scene fit into the fracture with micrometer perfection!

The thief confessed, and the jewels were restored, demonstrating that patient tracking of small clues builds an unshakeable case.'
moral: A broken fragment matching its origin speaks with unbreakable certainty in the hall of justice.
